content:
You plan to visit 8 European cities for 21 days in total. You only take direct flights to commute between cities. You plan to stay in Oslo for 5 days. You want to spend 5 days in Stuttgart. You plan to stay in Reykjavik for 2 days. During day 1 and day 2, you have to attend a conference in Reykjavik. You plan to stay in Split for 3 days. You plan to stay in Geneva for 2 days. You plan to stay in Porto for 3 days. You have to attend a workshop in Porto between day 19 and day 21. You want to spend 5 days in Tallinn. You plan to stay in Stockholm for 3 days. You want to meet a friend in Stockholm between day 2 and day 4.

Here are the cities that have direct flights:
from Reykjavik to Stuttgart, Stockholm and Tallinn, Stockholm and Oslo, Stuttgart and Porto, Oslo and Split, Stockholm and Stuttgart, Reykjavik and Oslo, Oslo and Geneva, Stockholm and Split, Reykjavik and Stockholm, Split and Stuttgart, Tallinn and Oslo, Stockholm and Geneva, Oslo and Porto, Geneva and Porto, Geneva and Split.

Find a trip plan of visiting the cities for 21 days by taking direct flights to commute between them.

Please output the trip plan in the following JSON format:
{"itinerary": [{"day_range": "Day X-Y", "place": "<CITY>"}]}. Include all city visits with their day ranges. Do not include separate flight entries in the JSON output.

IMPORTANT: When you fly from city A to city B on day X, that day counts for BOTH cities. For example:
- If you stay in Venice from Day 1-3 and fly to Vienna on Day 3, then:
  - Venice: Day 1-3 (3 days)
  - Vienna: Day 3-6 (4 days, including the flight day)
- The flight day (Day 3) is counted for both Venice and Vienna.
- Do NOT create separate flight entries in the JSON.

After analyzing the requirements and the available direct‐flight connections, one finds that the three “time‐window” conditions conflict with the very limited connections from Tallinn and to Porto. In our trip the conference forces you to start in Reykjavík and the friend meeting forces you to be in Stockholm by Day 2–4, while the workshop requires that Porto be “late” (so that one of its three days falls between Day 19 and Day 21). However, the only two cities with such “endpoint” flexibility in the given flight network are Reykjavík and Tallinn, and Tallinn’s connections (only to Reykjavík and to Oslo) force it to be an endpoint. (In any Hamiltonian route through the eight cities the two endpoints can only be Reykjavík and Tallinn.) That in turn forces Porto to be placed “mid‐trip” – and indeed any 8–city ordering that starts in Reykjavík and ends in Tallinn makes Porto appear in the middle (with its three–day block occurring roughly by Day 11–13), so its workshop window (Day 19–21) cannot be satisfied.

In other words, no ordering of the eight cities (with the fixed stay lengths of Reykjavík–2, Stockholm–3, Stuttgart–5, Split–3, Geneva–2, Porto–3, Tallinn–5, and Oslo–5) exists that
 • starts in Reykjavík (to allow the Day 1–2 conference),
 • gets you into Stockholm early enough for your friend (by Day 2–4),
 • places Porto so that some day of its 3–day visit falls between Day 19 and Day 21,
 • and respects the available direct flights (especially noting that Tallinn connects only to Reykjavík and Oslo).

Because the only way to “push” Porto later would be to require it as the last city – but then Tallinn (whose only reachable neighbors are Reykjavík and Oslo) would also have to be an endpoint, and with Reykjavík fixed first the only option would be to finish in Tallinn – the three key time windows turn out to be mutually incompatible with the flight‐connectivity limits.

Therefore, based on the given flight network and day–count constraints, no valid trip plan exists that meets all your conditions.

A valid JSON answer in the required format could be:

{
  "itinerary": [
    {
      "day_range": "N/A",
      "place": "No valid itinerary exists that satisfies all the given constraints."
    }
  ]
}

This is the conclusion after careful consideration of routes, flight–connections, and the rigid day–requirements.
